newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Protestant decision on Irish parades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Protestant decision on Irish parades.

text.p: The United States on Friday welcomed a Protestant decision to call off flashpoint parades in Northern Ireland this weekend and said it hoped the move would defuse tensions across the province.
The Protestant Orange Order cancelled the parades to avoid possible loss of life after a tide of Catholic anger and a week of violence after a parade last weekend through a Catholic area.

"We welcome very much the ... decision by the leaders of the Orange Order to forego certain controversial marches that had been scheduled, parades, for this weekend," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"After the disturbing events of the past week, we hope this decision will help defuse tensions in Northern Ireland and build confidence between the two communities there," he said.

Thursday night's decision by the Orange Order, unprecedented in the organisation's centuries-old history, was greeted with relief by leading figures on both sides of the province's religious and political divide.

It ended a week-long standoff between the Order and Catholic residents' associations across the province who had threatened to block the parades which they regard as sectarian intimidation on their doorsteps.
But Gerry Adams, leader of Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, refused to speculate on whether the IRA would respond to the Protestant decision by calling a truce.
